*It's the sixties of the nineteenth century now. You, the child of a rich businessman, set off for Africa to have a lovely vacation in exotic lands. And it was wonderful indeed! With a group of hunters you had fun, enjoying the beautiful landscapes of the savannah, watching predators hunting and herbivores running away. Your friends would burn in envy! Especially if you told them about local brutal men and their no lees gorgeous women. Oh, you spent hours watching them! At a distance, of course. Though, it seemed fate wanted you to take a closer look...*
*As your wish to admire Africa reached it's peak, you left your companions who didn't want to go further. You spent all the day walking around the savannah, this beautiful faraway land. Enjoying the sights, you went further and further, until you realised... that you got lost. After several hours of futile attempts to reunite with your companions, tiredness washed over you. In this state you couldn't continue your search. You were exhausted, both physically and mentally.*
*After a couple of hours, you found a small river hidden in lavish bushes. If course, you would rather prefer to have a soft bed instead, but it was tolerable. And just when you lay down on the ground, you suddenly noticed the rustle of the bushes. At first you thought this were predators. Your body tensed, ready to run away in every moment. But then you heard somebody's grunt. Soon, a black woman carrying a basket, came out of the bushes. Hope sparkled in your chest at the sight of her. You smiled widely, hoping the woman would help you.  Fortunately, your interest in African peoples was so great that you could speak some of the local languages fluently.*
*While recalling some local dialects, you was trying to show the woman that you had no intentions to hurt her. But before you could say anything, she suddenly put the basket on the ground, lunged forward and landed a solid punch on your stomach. Actually, it wasn't as painful as it could be - you were more confused than scared. But still, such reaction made you wonder about her motivation, especially when her face took an expression of pure hatred.*
